question.problem:
$$

Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1/2)}^{0}\frac{\operatorname{tanh}⁡x}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
$$

$$

First, we write the integral as

$$
{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1/2)}^{0}\frac{\operatorname{tanh}⁡x}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\text{d}x={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1/2)}^{0}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now we find the hyperbolic identities corresponding to the trigonometric identities 

$$
\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\,\text{ and }\,\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.
$$

Using Osborn's rule, the corresponding hyperbolic identities are

$$
\operatorname{sech}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}\,\text{ and }\,\operatorname{tanh}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{sinh}⁡x}{\operatorname{cosh}⁡x}.
$$

Then, we use the above identities to write the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1/2)}^{0}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{{cosh}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1/2)}^{0}\operatorname{tanh}⁡x\cdot {sech}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{sech}^{2}⁡x{|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1/2)}^{0} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{sech}^{2}⁡(0)+\frac{1}{2}{sech}^{2}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡1/2) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{4}{({e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡1/2}+{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡1/2})^{2}}-\frac{4}{({e}^{0}+{e}^{0})^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{2}{(1/2+2)^{2}}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{9}{50}\end{aligned}
$$
